Digitised from the vector content of Fig. 2 (page 16 of the report PDF): the time axis is calibrated on its 29 tick marks (every 25 h, 0 to 700 h), the value axis on its 7 gridlines (0 to 6 particle equivalents, 32.40 pt apart, no residual); least-squares time calibration, largest tick residual 0.25 h. Reading uncertainty +/-0.01 particle equivalents (the stored positions have a granularity of 0.12 pt = 0.004 equivalents, and the markers sit 0.004 above the axis at the zero line) and +/-0.3 h in time (tick granularity 0.24 pt = 0.5 h, so +/-0.25 h, plus the marker granularity). The unit is the average calculated particle inventory summed over the 75 particles (not a fraction per particle); the time-dependent data were scaled by the average deposition cup collection efficiency (printed p. 3). The source warns that the magnitude of the Cs release may be off because of the cup collection efficiency, that the plotted total Cs is less than three particles' worth although five failed TRISO particles are indicated, and that only about half of the Cs release is accounted for (printed p. 7). Elapsed time from the start of heating, the clock of the registered history AGR1-LP-4-4-2. Procedure, calibration and coordinates: audit log section 12.
